headline: Approved June 25, 2026 meeting minutes and discussed Main Streets, tourism, and economic development plan updates.
summary: The Council approved the June 25, 2026 meeting minutes. Members discussed the postponed Beverly Main Streets block party, Travel and Tourism Committee outreach plans, and public communication strategies for the completed Economic Development Action Plan (EDAP), including transit and parking priorities.
decisions: Approved the June 25, 2026 meeting minutes as presented; the Council was unanimously in favor.

2. Beverly Main Streets Update 27 
 28 
There was discussion regarding the postponement of the block party which was planned. 29 
Schaeffer explained that there were some recent staff changes and it was determined that there 30 
was likely neither the staffing nor the funding available to host a block party at this time. There 31 
are holiday stroll and restaurant week events planned later this year. Beverly Main Streets has 32 
long been volunteer-run and continues to determine what their future obligations will be. There 33 
was a question as to whether Beverly Main Streets should be an ECDC priority. Schaeffer stated 34 
that there are some things that could lead to partnerships with other entities. There was 35 
discussion regarding how to make some of the events profitable in order to continue to run them 36 
into the future. 37

how to draw people into Beverly. Other communities have destination nonprofit organizations 43 
that work to bring people into their towns. Beverly has Beverly Main Streets which works on 44

4. Economic Development Action Plan (EDAP) 51 
 a. Discussion of public communication tools to present EDAP 52 
 53 
Schaeffer stated that the EDAP was completed and is available on the City’s website. There was 54 
discussion that the plan is very robust and could be made more accessible from a bystander level. 55 
Distribution of materials will continue to be pursued. The completion of the plan could be 56

also be made available on the website. 59

 b. Strategizing priorities 61 
 62 
Wynne explained that the Beverly Shuttle and Council on Aging are working on a two-day per 63 
week shuttle run for some users. Some results of a recent survey showed that people may be 64 
using the shuttle to get to work. The hope is to use the survey data to explore potential future 65 
grant or other funding options for transit in the City. Recommendations could be made to the 66 
Mayor regarding other priority initiatives to consider. There was discussion regarding a parking 67 
initiative and working with the Tourism Committee on potential action items. Specific 68 
wayfinding for parking and other destinations around the City could also be considered. There 69 
was also discussion regarding how to make information on these topics more visible on the City 70 
website.  71
